clue.text: Chris kept at it, somehow purchasing large SPFL club

somehow says the letters get there by some unstated means, so their order must be reworked

parts.note: taken as written, thirteen letters of fodder
L is the standard abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Chris persevered with a big Scottish football club, perhaps buying a season ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: The SPFL is the Scottish Professional Football League; Partick Thistle is a Glasgow club in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Partick Thistle is a professional football team from Glasgow competing in Scotland's league system.

clue.text: Hierarchy in Beijing previously defending Communists' initial rule

explanation.definitionFit: A pecking order is a ranking of status within a group, named after the way hens establish dominance.

clue.text: Extremely rich author, we hear

parts.note: J. K. Rowling, the Harry Potter author

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain best-selling writer is fabulously wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, J. K. Rowling is herself extremely rich, which makes the surface true.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling, short for rolling in it or rolling in money, is an informal way of saying very wealthy.

clue.text: Put out lies regularly before taken to court

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of lies
to be sued is to be taken to court

explanation.surface: Someone published falsehoods regularly before ending up in court for libel.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a statement or publication is to put it out, release it to the public.

clue.text: Snatch a little sleep and I keep turning over

explanation.walkthrough: A little sleep looks like a nap or kip, but it is the hidden indicator; the answer lies backwards across four words.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to snatch or abduct them, usually for ransom.

clue.text: Unconventionally stylish types, what they wear?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fashionable people who follow trends outside the mainstream

definitions.note: the question mark marks the playful second sense
definitions.meaning: second meaning: trousers cut to sit on the hips rather than the waist

explanation.walkthrough: The clue jokes that trendy people wear garments sharing their name, which are called hipsters in Britain (hip-huggers in the US).
explanation.definitionFit: Hipsters are both trend-conscious people and low-slung trousers, so the word fits both halves of the clue.

clue.text: Cashews, nuts comprising centrepiece of store display

parts.note: middle letter of store

explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a glass case or setting for displaying items, so it is a display.

clue.text: Union numbers at intervals rapidly rising across Italy

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of rapidly

explanation.walkthrough: NOS, I and AIL together read upwards in the grid, giving SON, I and LIA from bottom to top.

clue.text: Visits about fifty localities on vacation

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

parts.note: first and last letters of localities

explanation.surface: Someone tours about fifty places while away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Calls are short visits, as when a person calls on a friend or a doctor makes house calls.

clue.text: Cricket tournament hosted by the same dull representative

explanation.walkthrough: The IPL is the Indian Premier League; 'the same' is ditto, written DO in lists.

clue.text: Temp Kerry has worked in huge retail outlets

parts.note: taken as written, twelve letters

clue.text: Suspect trainee mostly fills in time travelling

trainee without its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled trainee letters go between the I and N of IN, with T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant means moving from place to place, never settled, so it describes someone travelling.

clue.text: Comfortable with copper retiring

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
retiring means shy, reserved

explanation.surface: A policeman ready for retirement is comfortable with the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer and retiring a pension, but they are a chemical symbol and a shy temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job or life is easy and undemanding, so comfortable in the informal sense.

clue.text: Lady dismissed by singer is fatuous

taken as written, the part to remove

explanation.walkthrough: Lady looks like a woman being fired; it is the first half of the pop star's name, struck off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga means foolishly infatuated or senile, so silly and fatuous.

clue.text: Bearing gifts by the sound of it

parts.note: presents are gifts

explanation.surface: Someone carrying gifts, apparently, like a guest at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Bearing gifts suggests the Magi; bearing is the noun for how one carries oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence is a person's impressive manner or poise, which is what bearing means as a noun.

clue.text: Tie needing draw to keep one game up

I is the Roman numeral for one

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game

explanation.walkthrough: Tie and draw look like sporting results; tie is a binding cord and draw means entice.

clue.text: Pet cat, shell out for it

parts.note: a tortoiseshell is a cat with mottled black and orange fur
taken as written, the part to remove

explanation.walkthrough: Shell out looks like the idiom for paying; read separately, shell is dropped from the cat's name.

clue.text: Religious leader, 100, gives talk for long time

clue.text: Choice using reduced fat

clue.text: Common foe Will crushed

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Feast day after Saint Peregrine's, originally on second of May

parts.note: first letter of Peregrine

parts.note: second letter of May

a rap is a rebuke

clue.text: Capsized seamen escape adopting evacuation procedure

adopting means taking in, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.walkthrough: Evacuation suggests abandoning ship; here it means emptying the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema injects fluid into the rectum to empty the bowels, a medical procedure for evacuation.

clue.text: Work by essentially political cartoonist is excellent

clue.text: Coach two or three perhaps

definitions.note: examples of the noun prime, a prime number
definitions.meaning: second meaning: numbers divisible only by themselves and one
